narrative: The law school application was denied because the model estimated a 62% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—slightly more likely than not. That estimate placed you above the school’s risk threshold. The strongest factor was your third-year grade decile: you were in decile 3, while accepted students averaged about 5.79, so this lower standing pushed most strongly toward failure. Your family income bracket was the second-strongest factor and, in your case, also added to the failure risk; upper-middle income is shared by 45.4% of accepted students, but here it increased the estimated risk. Your first-year grade decile was third, with decile 3 versus an accepted average of 6, also pushing toward failure. Your LSAT of 34, below the accepted average of 37.18, and GPA of 3.10, below 3.23, were additional concerns but not among the top three. To proceed, ask admissions how to appeal or reapply, whether an explanatory statement or later academic work can be considered, and what bar-readiness evidence would help. Strengthen controllable factors such as LSAT preparation, additional coursework, and a clear explanation of your grade trend.
